summaryEn: Teaches you to state an intention with zu plus the infinitive, and where zu goes in a separable verb.
Teaches you to define a goal you can measure and to break it into steps.
Teaches you to choose between two courses by comparing them and to justify your choice.
Teaches you to talk about exam nerves with conditional clauses and to describe a strategy.
Teaches you to justify the aim of a training course with um … zu and to say what it is good for.
Teaches you to ask what you do not know about a university application, with indirect questions.
Teaches you to describe an experience in the past tense that written German uses.
Teaches you to describe your methods with paired conjunctions and to say which works best.
Teaches you to talk about making mistakes with clauses of contrast, and to keep your nerve.
Teaches you to give and to ask for advice in the subjunctive.
Teaches you to state your own opinion and to say whether you share someone else's.
Teaches you to weigh both sides of a question with paired conjunctions and to reach a conclusion.
Teaches you the soft patterns of objection that disagree without damaging the relationship.
Teaches you to give an opinion with verbs that take a fixed preposition and to answer conditionally.
Teaches you to doubt a claim and to dig into its source with an indirect question.
Teaches you to judge a production with clauses of contrast and to describe your expectations.
Teaches you to describe a book you have read with relative clauses and to recommend it.
Teaches you to compare tastes and to close a discussion politely.
Teaches you to describe the effect a work had on you, with verbs that take a fixed preposition.
Teaches you to line your arguments up and to close the talk with a conclusion.
Teaches you to describe an ongoing complaint with verbs that take a fixed preposition.
Teaches you to follow the referral and appointment process in passive sentences.
Teaches you to ask about taking medication with conditional clauses and to understand the answer.
Teaches you to describe your eating habits with infinitive phrases.
Teaches you to give and to take advice in the subjunctive.
Teaches you to describe the order of a day with the conjunctions bevor and während.
Teaches you to say that you are struggling and to ask for support, with fixed-preposition verbs.
Teaches you to tell what happened at the emergency department in order, pulling the earlier event back in time.
Teaches you to follow the vaccination process in passive sentences and to ask questions.
Teaches you to offer good wishes and help when you visit someone who is ill.
Teaches you to understand and ask about the rules for sorting rubbish, in passive sentences.
Teaches you to state the aim of an action with um … zu and to talk about saving.
Teaches you to weigh transport options with paired conjunctions and to defend your own choice.
Teaches you to describe products and shops with relative clauses and to explain your choice.
Teaches you to set out the rules of a shared project in passive sentences.
Teaches you to describe a change with comparative forms.
Teaches you to say why you volunteer and what it gives you.
Teaches you to describe the changes in a neighbourhood with the past passive.
Teaches you to say what you are there for, with a damit clause.
Teaches you to describe an animal with dative relative clauses and to talk about responsibility.
Teaches you to build a condition that is not real, with wäre and hätte.
Teaches you to express a wish that did not come true, with ich wünschte and würde.
Teaches you to express regret about the past, with hätte and the past participle.
Teaches you to name anxiety with conditional clauses and to put it in proportion.
Teaches you to tell of a friendship that broke and was rebuilt, in ordered past tenses.
Teaches you to soften a confession of feelings with the subjunctive.
Teaches you to talk through a disagreement without blame and to state the aim with damit.
Teaches you to describe a sense of belonging, tying it to the past with als.
Teaches you to describe a long-term dream with infinitive phrases and to break it into steps.
Teaches you to look back on your own learning and to look ahead to the next stage.
